label: D2 after choosing a1
explanation: Fires only at DELAY_2, and almost only when the agent just chose a1 (in_action == 1 at D2, so this is observed). It never fires at D1 or GO and almost never after a2 (0.2% of mass). Dev: P 0.87, R 0.99, F1 0.92, mass recall 1.00. Magnitude is largest when the previous trial was unrewarded: (D2 & a1 & prev_reward == 0) covers 91% of the top activation quartile at precision 0.96. It is also somewhat larger when S1 (the common state) is reached. Activations decay over runs of rewarded a1 trials, and most false positives (silent a1 D2 steps) come after reward streaks. Because a1 tends to be chosen when S1 is good, the feature correlates with good == S1, but the chosen action is what drives it.

issues: The claims hold. The feature is zero at D1 and GO. At D2, a2 holds only 0.2% of activation mass. The test split reproduces the reported scores (P 0.867, R 0.989, F1 0.924, mass recall 0.997).

Missed activations on test (1668 steps, 0.3% of mass) are tiny activations at a2 D2 steps, mostly just after an a1 trial. They look like leftover activity from the previous a1 trial and are scattered, not a systematic class.
False positives on test (23955 a1 D2 steps with no activation) mostly come after runs of rewarded a1 trials, as the explanation says. The label is still a fair summary.

'Larger when S1 is reached' is mainly about firing rate, not size. Among a1 D2 steps, precision is 0.917 when S1 is reached vs 0.726 for a rare S2. The top-quartile share for a1 & S1 (0.816) is only a little above its overall mass share (0.808). 'Somewhat' is fair.
The magnitude claim holds: a1 & D2 & prev_reward == 0 covers 90% of the top activation quartile at precision 0.956 (test).
Adding 'not after two rewarded a1 trials' raises precision to 0.90 but drops recall to 0.78 (F1 0.84), so the original predicate is better. No better predicate was found.
